What is F# and what is it used for?

F# is a strongly-typed, functional-first programming language on .NET. It combines functional programming (immutable data, type inference, pattern matching) with OOP and imperative features.

Used for: data science, finance, domain-driven design, web backends.

Tools: dotnet CLI, Visual Studio, Rider, VS Code with Ionide extension.

```bash
dotnet fsi hello.fsx        # run script
dotnet new console -lang F# -o HelloApp
cd HelloApp && dotnet run
```

How do let bindings, mutability, and type annotations work in F#?

```fsharp
// let bindings — immutable by default
let name = "Alice"
let age  = 30
let pi   = 3.14159

// Mutable — must be explicit
let mutable count = 0
count <- count + 1   // <- is the assignment operator for mutables

// Type annotations
let x : int    = 42
let y : float  = 3.14
let s : string = "hello"

// Primitive types
let i64 : int64  = 9000000000L
let f32 : float32= 3.14f
let dec : decimal= 19.99m
let ch  : char   = 'A'
```

Immutability by default is one of F#'s key safety features — you must opt in to mutability with `mutable`.

How do strings and string interpolation work in F#?

```fsharp
let str = "Hello, World!"
str.Length                   // 13
str.ToUpper()
str.Substring(0, 5)          // "Hello"
str.Contains("World")
str.Replace("World", "F#")
str.[0]                      // 'H' (char indexing)

// String interpolation (F# 5+)
let name = "Alice"
let age = 30
let greeting = $"Hello, {name}! Age: {age}"
let expr     = $"Double: {age * 2}"

// sprintf — type-safe formatting
let msg = sprintf "Name: %s, Age: %d, Pi: %.2f" name age 3.14
```

How do tuples and Option types work in F#?

```fsharp
// Tuple
let t = (1, "hello", 3.14)
let a, b, c = t        // destructuring
fst (1, 2)             // 1
snd (1, 2)             // 2

// Option — null-safe value
let some_val : int option = Some 42
let no_val   : int option = None

Option.get some_val                    // 42
Option.defaultValue 0 no_val           // 0
Option.map (fun x -> x * 2) some_val   // Some 84
Option.bind (fun x -> if x > 0 then Some x else None) some_val  // Some 42

// Pattern match on Option (idiomatic)
match some_val with
| Some v -> printfn "Got: %d" v
| None   -> printfn "Nothing"
```

`Option` replaces `null` — F# prevents null reference errors at compile time.

How do F# lists work and what are the key List module functions?

```fsharp
let lst = [1; 2; 3; 4; 5]
let lst2 = 0 :: lst        // prepend: [0;1;2;3;4;5]
let lst3 = lst @ [6; 7]   // append

List.head lst       // 1
List.tail lst       // [2;3;4;5]
List.last lst       // 5
List.length lst     // 5
List.item 2 lst     // 3 (0-indexed)

List.map (fun x -> x * 2) lst         // [2;4;6;8;10]
List.filter (fun x -> x % 2 = 0) lst  // [2;4]
List.fold (fun acc x -> acc + x) 0 lst // 15
List.reduce (+) lst                    // 15
List.sum lst                           // 15
List.sort lst
List.rev lst                           // [5;4;3;2;1]
List.take 3 lst                        // [1;2;3]
List.skip 2 lst                        // [3;4;5]
List.collect (fun x -> [x; x*2]) lst  // flatMap
List.zip lst lst                       // [(1,1);(2,2)...]
List.partition (fun x -> x % 2 = 0) lst  // ([2;4],[1;3;5])
```

How do arrays, sequences, maps, and sets work in F#?

```fsharp
// Array (mutable elements)
let arr = [| 1; 2; 3; 4; 5 |]
arr.[0]           // 1
arr.[0] <- 99     // mutate
Array.map ((*) 2) arr
Array.sort arr

// Sequence (lazy)
let seq1 = seq { 1 .. 10 }
Seq.take 5 (Seq.initInfinite id)  // [0;1;2;3;4]

// Map (immutable dictionary)
let m = Map.ofList [("Alice", 30); ("Bob", 25)]
m.["Alice"]                // 30
Map.find "Alice" m         // 30
Map.tryFind "Dave" m       // None
Map.add "Carol" 35 m
Map.containsKey "Alice" m  // true
Map.map (fun k v -> v + 1) m

// Set
let s = Set.ofList [1; 2; 3; 4; 5]
Set.contains 3 s            // true
Set.add 6 s
Set.union s (Set.ofList [4;5;6])
Set.intersect s (Set.ofList [3;4;5;6])
```

How do discriminated unions and records work in F#?

```fsharp
// Discriminated Union (ADT)
type Shape =
    | Circle    of radius : float
    | Rectangle of width : float * height : float
    | Triangle  of base_ : float * height : float

let area = function
    | Circle r         -> System.Math.PI * r * r
    | Rectangle(w, h)  -> w * h
    | Triangle(b, h)   -> 0.5 * b * h

// Recursive union
type Tree<'a> =
    | Leaf
    | Node of Tree<'a> * 'a * Tree<'a>

// Records
type Person = {
    Name : string
    Age  : int
    City : string
}

let alice = { Name = "Alice"; Age = 30; City = "NYC" }
alice.Name               // "Alice"
let older = { alice with Age = 31 }  // copy with update

// Record pattern matching
let greet { Name = n; Age = a } =
    sprintf "Hello %s, you are %d" n a
```

How do currying, partial application, and function composition work in F#?

```fsharp
// All functions are curried
let add a b = a + b
let add3 = add 3          // partial application
add3 7                     // 10

let multiply x y = x * y
let double = multiply 2
double 5   // 10

// Pipe operator |>
[1 .. 10]
|> List.filter (fun x -> x % 2 = 0)
|> List.map (fun x -> x * x)
|> List.sum               // 220

// Function composition >>
let incThenDouble = (+) 1 >> (*) 2
incThenDouble 5   // 12  ((5+1)*2)

let doubleThenInc = (*) 2 >> (+) 1
doubleThenInc 5   // 11  (5*2+1)
```

How does the MailboxProcessor (actor model) work in F#?

```fsharp
// MailboxProcessor — actor model for concurrent state
let counter =
    MailboxProcessor.Start(fun inbox ->
        let rec loop n = async {
            let! msg = inbox.Receive()
            match msg with
            | "inc" -> return! loop (n + 1)
            | "get" ->
                inbox.Reply(n)
                return! loop n
            | _ -> return ()
        }
        loop 0)

counter.Post "inc"
counter.Post "inc"
let v = counter.PostAndReply (fun r -> "get")   // 2
```

MailboxProcessor is F#'s built-in actor model — each processor has a private message queue and processes messages sequentially, making state management thread-safe without locks.

How do measure types (physical units) work in F#?

```fsharp
[<Measure>] type m
[<Measure>] type s
[<Measure>] type kg

let distance = 100.0<m>
let time     = 10.0<s>
let speed    = distance / time   // 10.0<m/s>  (type-checked!)

let mass  = 70.0<kg>
let accel = 9.81<m/s^2>
let force = mass * accel         // 686.7<kg m/s^2> = Newtons

// Type error caught at compile time:
// let wrong = distance + time  // ERROR: m ≠ s
```

Measure types add **physical units** to the type system — you get a compile-time error if you accidentally add meters to seconds. Zero runtime overhead.

How do interfaces and OOP work in F#?

```fsharp
type IAnimal =
    abstract member Name  : string
    abstract member Speak : unit -> string

type Dog(name : string) =
    interface IAnimal with
        member _.Name = name
        member _.Speak() = "Woof!"
    member _.Fetch() = sprintf "%s fetches!" name

let dog = Dog("Rex")
let animal = dog :> IAnimal   // upcast to interface
animal.Speak()   // "Woof!"
dog.Fetch()      // "Rex fetches!"

// Class with mutable state
type Counter(initial : int) =
    let mutable count = initial
    member _.Value = count
    member _.Increment() =
        count <- count + 1
        count
    member _.Reset() = count <- initial

let c = Counter(0)
c.Increment() |> ignore
c.Increment() |> ignore
c.Value   // 2
```
